Question: What is the remainder when \[3^0+3^1+3^2+\cdots+3^{2009}\] is divided by \(8?\)
Solution:
Successive powers of \(3\) have a short remainder pattern when divided by \(8\). The first power is \(3^0=1\). Multiplying a number with remainder \(1\) by \(3\) gives remainder \(3\); multiplying a number with remainder \(3\) by \(3\) gives remainder \(1\), since \(9=8+1\). Thus the remainders alternate
\[
1,3,1,3,\ldots.
\]
There are \(2009-0+1=2010\) terms, so we can group all of them into \(1005\) consecutive pairs. Each pair has the same remainder as \(1+3=4\). Replacing every pair by \(4\) changes the sum only by a multiple of \(8\), so the required remainder is the remainder of
\[
1005\cdot4=4020=8\cdot502+4.
\]
It is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
